## Breaking Change:

No breaking.

## Description:

Experiments showed that timing of websocket requests to the Vallox firmware is
critical when fetching new metrics. Tests on different Raspberry Pis and x86
machines showed that those machines with little processing power tend to fail
the timing requirments during the busy startup phase of Home Assistant,
resulting in the Vallox integration failing to set itself up.

This patch catches Websocket's InvalidMessage, which is a symptom of failing the
timing requirements. Experiments again showed that on the Raspberrys, this
exception is catched once at startup, but the integration is running fine
afterwards.

Issue discussion and tests on:
  - https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues/25335
  - https://community.home-assistant.io/t/vallox-valloplus-350mv-partial-success-work-in-progress-on-vallox-component/52588/30

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #25335

**Pull request with documentation for [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io) (if applicable):** N/A

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml` (if applicable):
```yaml
vallox:
  host: IP
```

Sent you the tcpdump via email.

I am on raspbian now. Here, it _always_ fails.

In summary:
RPi3, hassio, aarch64 kernel: Fails 50% of time.
RPi3, raspbian, armv7l kernel: Fails 100% of time.
x86: Works 100% of time.

Did you had a chance to run my test file? Does it work on your raspberry?
I use xbian on raspberry. Test file works ok on that.

In your TCP Dump there is strange delay in TCP connection. Your raspberry does not send anything to the socket for a second after initial connection, so vallox asks to close the connection. Then raspberry tries to send data to a closed socket but valox already responds with connection reset.

Hmm, this would be an additional clue that this might be a processing power issue?

The armv7l RPi3 I tested on runs on 1200 MHz because it is version V1.2 B.
The aarch64 one is already version B+, running at 1400 MHz.
And the x86 machine is more potent in processing power anyways.

So with decreasing processing power we see increase in failure rate. Could it be that on Home Assistant boot, the less potent processors are overloaded and cannot send the next packet in time?

So my current approach is [to catch the exception](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/vallox-valloplus-350mv-partial-success-work-in-progress-on-vallox-component/52588/36). It is caught only once during the busy startup phase of Home Assistant and never shows up again afterwards.
Is it possible to delay the startup?
Tried it with a sleep first, but Home Assistant runtime complains if the setup time of a component takes too long.
`asyncio.sleep`?
Yes, the runtime still caught it.
But maybe you can split your initial setup into parts and fetch metrics in loop.call_later? With a sleep? I would try that path.

If you remove this line, or schedule it for later? Will it be bad?
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/56b8da133c53e722ec412497af723a0bb39bef74/homeassistant/components/vallox/__init__.py#L114

> If you remove this line, or schedule it for later? Will it be bad?
> https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/56b8da133c53e722ec412497af723a0bb39bef74/homeassistant/components/vallox/__init__.py#L114

I made this change already locally, after posting to the forum :)
Does not resolve the issue, unfortunately. The first call to `async_update()` arrives too soon.

In the end, catching this error makes the whole integration more robust anyways. In the current state in upstream, the integration would die and a reboot would be necessary whenever a connection gets reset. By catching the exception, the system at least stays alive and all the sensors in the GUI clearly indicate that something went wrong because they get greyed out after the valid state is set to false.
And chances are high that the next poll succeeds again, and the integration recovers without reboot.

Would probably be worth thinking about catching even more errors than just `InvalidMessage`.

Doesn't this also trigger initial update?
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/236820d093a9d79d99b1055108dede7395639c97/homeassistant/components/vallox/sensor.py#L93
Oh, you are right! Good catch. I changed those as well. Now on my faster RPi, even the initial fault is gone.
